# NPU18016

NPU18016 is an NPU code — a standardized laboratory coding identifier — used for the measurement of plasma creatinine (P-creatinin) [^src1]. Within the Danish clinical registry context, this specific code is notable for its uneven geographic use: it is predominantly applied in two regions, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] [^src1].

The code appears in the 2024 annual report of the Danish national clinical quality program for atrial fibrillation (Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram for atrieflimren), in a section discussing Indicator 4b, which tracks P-creatinin measurement among patients treated with DOACs (direct oral anticoagulants), and Indicator 5, covering the incidence of ischemic stroke [^src1]. That section documents regional and cluster-based variation in how well quality standards are met across Denmark, drawing on data from national registries including the Landspatientregisteret (National Patient Registry), Lægemiddelstatistikregisteret (Medicine Statistics Registry), and the Laboratorieregistret (Laboratory Registry) [^src1]. Region Nordjylland was identified as the best performer on Indicator 4b [^src1]. The broader discussion in this part of the report addresses the need for better monitoring of kidney function in DOAC patients and improved communication between hospitals and primary care [^src1].

Because P-creatinin measurement can be recorded under different NPU codes depending on which laboratory system a region uses, the fact that NPU18016 is concentrated in Region Syddanmark and Region Nordjylland is a data-quality detail relevant to interpreting national indicator results — it signals that comparisons across regions may need to account for coding differences rather than assuming a single uniform code is used everywhere [^src1].
